prompts.text: What small classroom adjustment can make learning easier for a wider range of students?
Describe a time a teacher found another way to include somebody in an activity.
Provide lesson notes in several formats or allow more choices in how students demonstrate learning?
A school wants to redesign its study area for students with different sensory needs. What should it ask first?
An adjustment that helps one learner often makes a lesson clearer for many others.
Accessible teaching should be considered during planning rather than added only after someone struggles.
Which feature of a classroom would you improve to reduce unnecessary distractions?
Recall learning effectively because somebody gave you additional time or a different explanation.
A school receives funding for one accessibility improvement. How could students help assess priorities?
Offer quiet spaces for focused work or varied ways for students to participate in discussions?
What did school uniforms change about the way students expressed themselves?
Tell me about a dress-code rule that students interpreted in an unexpected way.
Let students choose from several practical uniform options or use a simple colour-based dress code?
A school is reviewing its dress code with parents and students. Whose experiences should it hear?
Rules about clothing can affect comfort, affordability and belonging in different ways.
A school dress policy should be judged by its practical effects, not just how tidy it looks.
Which detail of your old school uniform do you remember most clearly?
Recall a school event when everybody was allowed to wear something other than their usual uniform.
Students want a dress policy that suits hot weather. What questions should the school consider?
Choose comfortable sportswear for activity days or keep a flexible everyday uniform?
What is the most interesting way a language teacher has helped you understand an expression?
Recall learning a word that didn't translate neatly into your first language.
Learn a new language through conversation games or by reading short stories?
A class includes students who speak several home languages. How might they share this knowledge respectfully?
Multilingual classrooms can connect language lessons to the way people communicate at home.
Understanding a phrase's context matters more than translating its words perfectly.
Which school subject would you enjoy studying partly through another language?
Describe the first time you understood a conversation using a language you were learning.
A student wants to practise speaking without fear of embarrassment. What classroom activity might help?
Create a bilingual school newsletter or host an informal language-exchange afternoon?
Which artistic activity helped you understand a subject that wasn't usually considered creative?
Tell me about a school performance that taught you more than you expected.
Design a history exhibit with illustrations or explain a science idea through a short play?
A teacher wants to combine music and mathematics for one lesson. What could students explore?
Creative projects can reveal how students understand ideas beyond memorised definitions.
Artistic subjects deserve attention even when students plan careers in other fields.
What's a creative assignment you still remember because you enjoyed making it?
Recall an unexpected compliment for something you created at school.
You're organising a student showcase with very little equipment. How would you let different talents appear?
Make a short documentary about school life or produce an illustrated community history booklet?
What made a school lunch break feel like a real break rather than another scheduled task?
Describe a favourite lunch-time routine with classmates.
Give students more outdoor space to eat or create quieter indoor lunch areas?
A school wants to improve its lunch arrangements without increasing costs much. What would you ask students?
The way breaks are organised affects friendships as well as concentration.
Unstructured time can be an important part of a school day.
What simple change would have improved your lunch experience at school?
Recall a funny moment around a shared snack or school meal.
Students want a more practical system for bringing lunches from home. What might help?
A longer lunch break or several shorter breaks spread through the day?
Which school field trip helped you see a familiar subject differently?
Tell me about visiting a place for an assignment and noticing something beyond the lesson.
Take a class to a local museum or invite a practitioner to demonstrate their work at school?
A teacher wants to organise a meaningful trip with a limited budget. Where might they start?
Real-world examples can make classroom concepts feel more relevant.
A nearby field trip can be just as educational as an expensive journey.
Which local business or community service would make an interesting place for students to learn?
Recall a school outing when another student's question made everyone think.
Students are visiting a public park to study the environment. What would make the visit more than a walk?
Explore a local heritage site with a guide or conduct a simple neighbourhood survey?
What basic spending decision could help students learn about budgeting without using real money?
Describe a school project that taught you to plan resources carefully.
Run a pretend shop for one lesson or plan a class event with a fixed fictional budget?
A group must organise a small exhibition with shared materials. How should they decide what to buy?
Class projects reveal how limited resources can encourage creative problem-solving.
Practical money lessons should allow students to make mistakes safely.
Which school activity would teach the most about the difference between needs and wants?
Recall a teacher explaining a practical cost that surprised the class.
Students want to raise funds for a library project. What should they learn before asking for contributions?
Compare prices for a class project or design a simple savings goal together?
What environmental change at your school would have made daily life more pleasant?
Tell me about a classroom or school garden project that gave students responsibility.
Introduce a composting project or plant shade trees around the playground?
A school wants students to investigate water use. What could they measure without special equipment?
Small environmental habits become easier when students understand their practical benefits.
School sustainability projects should teach real measurement rather than just display slogans.
Which local environmental issue would make a good student research project?
Recall discovering something unexpected about plants, insects or weather during a school activity.
Students want to improve waste sorting but the current bins confuse everyone. What would help?
Explore how rainfall affects the school grounds or track how much paper a class uses?
How should students be able to suggest changes to ordinary school routines?
Recall a school representative who listened to classmates rather than speaking for them.
Collect anonymous suggestions or hold short open meetings with elected representatives?
Students disagree about whether to extend library hours. How should their views be gathered fairly?
Student councils teach more when members can explain decisions as well as make proposals.
Young people can contribute useful ideas about rules they experience every day.
What's a school policy you would want students to help review?
Describe a time a school listened to a practical concern raised by students.
A student group wants more recreational space but other needs compete for funding. How could they make a case?
Let students propose small improvement projects or join staff discussions on existing plans?
What do you think schools should teach about deciding whether online information is reliable?
Tell me about an occasion when checking a source changed your understanding of a topic.
Practise spotting misleading headlines or learn how to verify a claim using several sources?
An AI tool gives two students different explanations for the same question. How should their teacher respond?
Easy access to information makes evaluating it more important, not less.
Digital literacy includes knowing when to put a tool aside and think independently.
Which task would you prefer students to learn without relying on automation first?
Recall using technology to explore a subject that would once have been difficult to study.
Your school is designing a responsible AI-use policy for assignments. Which principle belongs at the top?
Explore how an AI model can make mistakes or practise writing clearer questions for digital tools?
